title: Runtime: load and apply quantization profile (artifacts, kernel selection, metrics/logging)
creator: Mateo Alvarez
description:
Goal
Ship runtime support for route-level quantization profiles: deterministically load a resolved profile artifact, apply the quantization mode + kernel path safely, and emit high-signal metrics/logs/traces so rollouts can be monitored and rolled back.

Background
Control plane will resolve a route’s quantization_profile_ref to a concrete, versioned profile_id (or "disabled" / "fallback") after compatibility checks. Runtime must:
- Treat the resolved profile_id as an input to execution planning.
- Load artifacts (weights format, scales, metadata) in a cache-friendly + rate-limited way.
- Select supported kernels (including mixed INT8/FP8 paths) and guard against unsupported combinations.
- Surface applied vs fallback/disabled state for every request and aggregate it at route/model/region.

Design links
- Runtime design: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture/quantization-profile-selection-in-runtime.json
- Compatibility/fallback standard: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/quantization-profile-compatibility-and-fallbacks.json
- Control plane config service: sources/confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/quantization-profile-config-service.json
- Perf suite: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/quantization-profile-perf-benchmark-suite.json

Scope (v1)
1) Profile resolution input
- Accept resolved fields from routing/control plane on the request context:
  - quant_profile_id (opaque, versioned)
  - quant_profile_resolution (applied|disabled|fallback)
  - quant_profile_fallback_reason (optional, bounded cardinality)
- Determinism requirement: the same request context must lead to the same quant mode decision (no "latest" resolution inside runtime).

2) Artifact loading + caching
- Implement an artifact fetcher keyed by (model_id, model_variant, quant_profile_id) with:
  - in-process LRU cache for metadata + handles
  - background warmup on model load (best-effort)
  - strict timeouts and bounded retries; no blocking the decode hot path indefinitely
  - negative caching for known-missing or invalid profiles (short TTL)
- Ensure we do not thundering-herd the model registry under high QPS. (Follow-up ties into caching/rate limit work.)

3) Kernel selection and guardrails
- Integrate with kernel auto-selection to support:
  - INT8 weights + FP16 activations (baseline quant v1)
  - mixed FP8/INT8 paths where explicitly allowed by profile + GPU class
- Guardrails:
  - hard fail closed to baseline precision if a requested kernel path is unavailable
  - cap unsupported sequence lengths per profile metadata (e.g., max_context) and fallback cleanly
  - never attempt repeated fallback loops (single decision per request)

4) KV cache + memory interactions
- Verify KV cache format remains baseline unless profile explicitly changes KV precision (out of v1; must remain unchanged).
- Ensure prefix/KV caching keys incorporate quant_profile_id so we do not reuse cache entries across quant modes.

5) Observability
Emit:
- Request log annotations:
  - quant_profile_id
  - quant_profile_resolution
  - quant_profile_fallback_reason
- Metrics (names tentative; align with telemetry standards during implementation):
  - quant_profile_requests_total{route,model,region,resolution}
  - quant_profile_fallback_total{route,model,region,reason}
  - quant_profile_artifact_load_latency_ms{model,profile_id,cache_hit}
  - quant_profile_artifact_load_errors_total{model,profile_id,error_type}
  - decode_latency_ms / e2e_latency_ms with tag quant_enabled=true|false (sampled to avoid cardinality blowup)
- Tracing:
  - span attribute quant.profile_id
  - span event quant.profile.applied or quant.profile.fallback with reason

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Runtime deterministically applies quantization when quant_profile_id is present and compatible kernels exist.
- [x] On any incompatibility/missing artifacts/unsupported kernel path, runtime falls back to baseline precision and marks resolution=fallback with a reason.
- [x] No change in behavior when feature is off (resolution=disabled).
- [x] KV/prefix cache safety: cache keys segregate baseline vs quantized.
- [x] Metrics/logs/traces make it possible to answer:
  - Is the profile applied for this request id?
  - What % of traffic is enabled vs fallback?
  - Are we seeing artifact load spikes/errors?
  - What’s the p95 decode latency delta?
- [x] Verified in perf-canary scenarios comparing baseline vs enabled with thresholds.

Implementation notes
- Decision point: runtime must not resolve aliases ("recommended", "latest"). Only accepts concrete profile_id from control plane.
- Artifact format: treat as immutable, content-addressed bundle; validate signature/hash before use.
- Reason codes (bounded): INCOMPATIBLE_GPU, INCOMPATIBLE_MODEL_VARIANT, SEQ_LEN_EXCEEDED, ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND, ARTIFACT_INVALID, KERNEL_UNSUPPORTED, KILL_SWITCH_ENABLED.

Testing plan
- Unit tests:
  - profile id present -> artifact load -> kernel selection -> applied
  - error paths (missing/invalid artifact, unsupported kernel) -> fallback with reason
  - cache key segregation baseline vs quantized
- Integration tests:
  - control plane provides resolved profile id; runtime applies and emits quant_profile_id
- Perf:
  - run suite across A10/L4/H100 classes; measure cost/token + p95 decode latency

Rollout notes
- Must honor global kill-switch (platform-level); runtime should treat kill-switch as resolution=fallback with reason=KILL_SWITCH_ENABLED (or disabled depending on policy input).
- Canary strategy: enable for perf-canary and 1% design partner traffic with explicit rollback if fallback_rate or latency regression exceeds thresholds.

Links / related PRs
- sources/github/redwood/pr-18463-runtime-load-quantization-profile-and-emit-metrics.json
- sources/github/redwood/pr-18479-runtime-kernel-selection-updates-for-int8-fp8-mix.json
- sources/github/redwood/pr-18555-add-runtime-log-annotation-quant_profile_id.json
- sources/github/redwood/pr-18531-fix-fallback-loop-when-profile-incompatible.json
- sources/github/redwood/pr-18547-rate-limit-protection-for-profile-metadata-fetch.json

Open questions (resolved)
- Do we allow runtime to auto-resolve "recommended"? -> No; only control plane resolves. (Determinism + change control.)
- Should fallback be silent? -> No; must be observable via metrics/log annotation and reason code.

Risks
- Cardinality explosion if we tag metrics with profile_id broadly. Mitigation: profile_id only on logs/traces and limited error metrics; aggregate metrics keyed by route/model/region/resolution.
- Artifact fetch on cold start impacting tail latency. Mitigation: warmup + strict timeouts + cache.

comments: 2025-01-24 (Noah Patel): Started implementation with a minimal artifact loader + request-context wiring. Confirming with Platform that runtime will never resolve aliases; we will only accept a concrete profile_id.
2025-01-30 (Hiro Tanaka): Kernel selection changes needed for mixed FP8/INT8 path; adding guards for unsupported SM versions and max context constraints. Will post microbench results in PR.

2025-02-04 (Omar El-Sayed): KV cache must remain baseline in v1. Please ensure cache key includes quant_profile_id (or a quant_enabled bit) to avoid cross-mode reuse. Also watch for prefix-cache collisions.

2025-02-10 (Noah Patel): Added fallback reason codes and ensured single-decision behavior (no repeated fallback attempts). Found an edge case where policy looped on incompatible profile; patched in follow-up.

2025-02-21 (Sofia Ivanova): Scheduling/batching path looks safe as long as quant mode is part of the batch signature. Please ensure mixed quant/non-quant requests do not co-batch unless identical execution plan.
2025-03-03 (Leila Farouk): E2E test plan ok; please add an integration test that asserts quant_profile_id is present in runtime logs for a known request id (smoke signal for Support).
2025-03-12 (Connor O'Brien): Release train note: ship behind kill-switch default OFF + allowlist. Canary in perf-canary required before enabling any design partner.
2025-03-18 (Noah Patel): Landed all PRs; perf-canary green. Observability tags are sampled for latency histograms to avoid cardinality. Docs for reason codes added to internal runtime runbook notes.
